title: Causal machine learning finds who responds to loss or gain framing in retirement saving
summary: In a large randomized field experiment with a European retirement savings company, causal machine learning estimated who responds to loss-framed versus gain-framed reminders, and the estimates were validated in a second independent experiment. In that validation, conversion was estimated to rise 9.4 percentage points for the 25% most responsive to loss framing and fall 8.4 points for the 25% most responsive to gain framing. A personalized targeting policy was expected to raise participation from 4.53% to 6.86% and average savings from EUR 2,062 to EUR 2,442 per converted customer relative to uniform loss framing. Behavioral-economics result from one company; the sample sizes are not legible in the abstract.
ai_technology: Causal machine learning estimating heterogeneous treatment effects across socioeconomic characteristics

evidence.tested: Heterogeneous framing effects estimated in one randomized field experiment and validated in a second independent experiment.
evidence.unknown: Sample sizes, model details and generalization beyond one European retirement savings company; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Causal machine learning estimated heterogeneous treatment effects and a targeting policy.
